# /crav1-build-walk

lane: build | group: Build | starter: no | stage: stable | since: 1.142.0 | prompts: 4
purpose: Walk one work branch from build through merge, with one Next while it runs.
use_when: A ready slice should be built one work branch at a time, through the pull request and the merge
reads: Reads `spec.md`, `plan.md`, `tasks.md`, `build-map.md`, `claims.md` when it exists, and this branch's `build-progress` file. It fetches the specs repo before it reads. The branch offer is `scripts/build_map.py docs/specs/<slug> --recommend T#` through `scripts/build_walk.py`. It reads the pull request author and the branch's commit authors before other-owner mode.
writes: Writes `docs/specs/<slug>/build-progress/<branch>.md` after yes, with normalized hashes and `Content stamp: normalized`, and commits that file after the yes. When the step already commits other files, the progress file is in that same commit. Otherwise it is its own commit, using the persisted commit style. Nothing is pushed until the end-of-walk card, or the claim card, except on a whole-branch run, where the start yes covers a push after each task and the `## Run` section records each built task. Writes `docs/specs/<slug>/claims.md` when the walk starts on a branch, and commits and pushes only that file after yes. Writes `(live yes: <name>, <date>)` on the task line after the live yes. Posts one pull request comment per push in other-owner mode, after yes.
leaves alone: Leaves `spec.md` alone except that live-yes note. Does not tick a row itself. Does not push, open, or merge before `yes`. Does not overwrite another user's `In progress:` claim. Does not edit another owner's pull request description unless this run said `edit-description`. Never rebases.
limits: A headless run stops before any step. An unnamed current user is not a switch. A merged or deleted branch is not offered. An unapproved Approval needed item is not built. An `Approved:` line does not run the live change. Other-owner mode does not open, merge the base, or merge the pull request. It is not a starter option.
flow:
- `claims.py preserve --write` keeps claimed rows in their tasks.md order, not the claims.md order, and keeps the file's line endings.
- `branch_run.py plan` labels a task with its short title from `verify.md` (else the map name, never cut with dots); the full name stays in `full` for the ending.
- `branch_run.py record` keeps the specs repo (`--specs-repo`, default the top level of `--root`) and the code repo (`--code-repo`) apart, checks both before writing, commits `verify.md` with the progress file and the work-item mention, and pushes both.
- `branch_run.py ending --root --branch` reads `build-progress/<branch>.md` itself, takes `--note` lines for `Before the merge:`, and accepts a plain `stop`.
- the walk ending and the whole-branch ending put a plain label above the command, such as `Build T3 Record the decision on feat/orders-api:` above `/crav1-build-walk orders-api T3`, never a lowercase line under it.
- `branch_run.py ending` accepts a plain `stop` value such as `"merge"`.
- the build walk is offered to continue only by its own claim user, the name `git config user.name` gives; `Owner: self` in a progress file is never trusted alone.
- Someone else's built walk is a Waiting line such as `T9 to T12 are person B's, built, and wait for PR 82 to merge.`
- a specs repo that is behind or diverged ends with a label line above the command, `Merge origin into your local branch, since they have diverged (never rebase):` (or `since it is behind`), then `git pull --no-rebase` alone in its code span.
- `build_walk.py next --root <spec folder> --branch <branch>` builds the walk state itself: phase, owner and pull request from `build-progress/<branch>.md`, full task names from `tasks.md`, the Uncommitted line from `git status`.
- `build_walk.py progress init` and `progress record --step <step> --result <result> --yes` write the progress file with `Done` and the normalized stamps; without `--yes` they preview.
- At `comment` or `wait-merge` the walk prints `lead` and `ending` straight from the script and reads no reference.
- The one-task build skips `tool-approvals.md` when the walk passes `approvals: already-done`.
- The `next` output has `lead`, one sentence from phase and owner (`T5 is pushed to PR 71 and waits for its merge.`) that agrees with the Uncommitted line; print only that before Run next.
- Two or more tasks use the branch form `/crav1-build-walk <slug> <branch>`, never a comma list.
- In other-owner mode a built and pushed task's verify row says `Implemented, verified, tick pending`.
- cards follow the card wording rule in `docs/reference/question-cards.md`: a plain question, each option saying what happens, the recommended one first with why.
- The other-owner card asks `Should I add my work to their pull request?`.
- Settle-and-push is one card: one yes commits the walk's files and pushes the specs repo.
- Waiting lines name who or what and why, for example `Waiting: person A to merge pull request 71, then the tasks on feat/orders-cicd are ticked.`
- `claims.py` writes `since` in local time with the local offset, to the second, for example `2026-11-14T23:40:00+01:00`; an older UTC line still reads.
- Your own claim does not hold a task in the ready check: `walk_progress.py readiness --root <spec-folder> --user <name> --branch <branch>` (user defaults to `git config user.name`) gives your claimed task `refused` false and `in progress by you`.
- the walk offer keeps a task-line branch that is only on origin, or is the head of an open pull request, and checks it out without a card when `--recommend` prints `checkout:`.
- **`/crav1-build-walk`** is one guided walk of one work branch.
- It opens `/crav1-build-tasks`, verify, `/crav1-finalize-commit`, `/crav1-open-pr`, the merge of the base into the branch, `/crav1-merge-pr`, and the tick, by file.
- Each step that writes, pushes, opens, or merges asks `yes` first.
- It never rebases.
- Other-owner mode, after `switch`, never opens a pull request, never merges the base in, and never merges or completes the pull request.
- It posts one comment per push and edits the description only on `edit-description`.
- A `(Runs live)` task gets a script, a dry run, then the user's own yes, recorded as `(live yes: <name>, <date>)`.
- An `Approved:` line does not replace that yes.
- on a `(Runs live)` task, a recorded yes that the assistant's permission check refused is not a missing yes.
- Next is `/crav1-build-walk` after the command has run.
- the next line is `scripts/build_walk.py next --json <file>`.
- A stack command is `scripts/build_walk.py stack --json <file>`.
- `--recommend` is `scripts/build_map.py docs/specs/<slug> --recommend T#`.
- On Windows the interpreter is `python` with `PYTHONUTF8=1`.
- Elsewhere it is `python3`.
- the reply prints `ending`.
- `Run next:` is first.
- Each command is alone in a code span and works in a new session: `/crav1-build-walk T3`, plus the slug when `docs/specs` has more than one slice.
- Another branch whose tasks can start, from readiness `can_start` grouped by build-map branch, is its own Run next entry.
- Recording a step commits `build-progress/<branch>.md` after yes, in the same commit when the step already commits other files, otherwise on its own, using the persisted commit style.
- `T27` and `27` are the same id.
- `next --json` accepts task strings or `{id, title}` objects.
- Bad input returns `{"ok": false, "code", "line"}`.
- Behind or diverged, it stops and Run next is `git pull --no-rebase`.
- When it starts on a branch it writes `In progress:` in `docs/specs/<slug>/claims.md` and, after yes, commits and pushes only that file.
- The ready check holds those tasks as `in progress by <user> since <date>` and does not offer them in Run next.
- `release-claim` clears the claim.
- A claim older than three days, or `Claim max age:`, warns and is never cleared on its own.
- `/crav1-build-walk <slug> <branch>` builds every open task on that branch in task order, in one run.
- `/crav1-build-walk <slug> T5` still builds one task.
- After one start yes the run claims every open task on the branch on one `In progress:` line, builds each task, runs its tests, commits it, records `- Built: T#, commit <sha>, tests <result>` in the `## Run` section of `build-progress/<branch>.md`, and pushes with no card.
- It prints one progress line per task, such as `T9 done, tests green, starting T10`, with a soft fresh-session hint every three tasks (`Fresh session hint: every N tasks`).
- It stops only for an open question on the next task, a stakeholder yes that is not recorded, a manual, secret, host-setup, or Runs live step, tests or lint still red after a fair try, a wanted change outside the task's scope, someone else's claim on or change to a run task (fetched before each task, merged in when only behind, never rebased), and always before the merge.
- Rerunning the same command resumes from `Next task:`, reuses its own claim, and builds nothing twice.
- The script is `scripts/branch_run.py`.
- each start and each recorded task also writes this branch's one status line in `walk-progress.md` (`- Branch run: feat/orders-cicd: running, T9 done, next T10 (<time>).
- Log: build-progress/feat--orders-cicd.md`), then `stopped before merge`, `stopped at T#: <why>`, or `merged` through `branch_run.py status`.
- The claim is cleared when the branch is merged or ticked, or the user says stop and is done with this walk, or `release-claim`.
- the in-walk and branch-run endings are built by the shared walk ending (`scripts/walk_ending.py`), so for the same ready branches the Run next entries match the ready check word for word.
- The script no longer writes a `Next:` line under it.
- A held step (an Approval needed item, a live yes, a pull request still to merge, someone else's branch) says why on a `Waiting:` line instead, and with no work branch left Run next is `/crav1-verify-build-against-spec`.
- The JSON `next` list still has one sentence per Run next entry, and is not printed.
- a second task on a branch whose progress file lists only the first is recorded: `build_walk.py progress record --step 'build T47'` accepts `build <task>` for any task and adds it to the header's Tasks: line, so the lead, the ending, the merge list (one PR ticks both) and the build map name both.
- Before the build step, `repo_sync.py code-behind --repo <code repo>` checks the code branch against origin; behind offers `fast-forward` or `stop` on a card and fast-forwards only after `fast-forward`, never silently.
- a progress file from an older kit that records a second task's build as a plain `- Step: build` with the task only in the result (`Result: done (T47: ...)`) counts that task too: the lead and the Waiting line name every task on the branch (`T43 and T47 are pushed to PR 73 and wait for its merge`), and the next write adds it to the header's Tasks: line.
- `/crav1-build-walk <slug> <T#>` starts an open, unclaimed task as new work even when the branch's other tasks wait for the merge; wait-merge applies only once every task is pushed.
- `build_walk.py next --task` returns `start`, and `progress start-task` claims the task, adds it to the header and records `start <T#>`.
- A task that cannot start gets a card and a Run next from the script.
- On another person's branch a take-in task (`(take-in: develop)`, or text that says it takes in develop) may merge the base into the branch with its own yes: `git merge --no-ff`, the whole suite and the linter, a push after yes and one comment; the pull request merge stays with its owner, and the ending names who merges.
- the task name in the lead, the ending under Run next and the yes card stops at the first verify item (`; integration —`, `; contract —`, `; system —`, `; unit —`, `(verify: ...`), so a task line with its checks shows only its name, such as `Build T8 PR 12 takes in develop after PR 10 merges, with the conflicts resolved on feat/orders-api:`.
- The one helper is `task_order.task_name`.
- the same helper drops a leading `` `fix/x` from `develop` `` clause and parenthesised marks such as `(manual, secret, …)`, so the label and the Tasks line are the outcome.
- `claims.py add` prints the line and leaves `claims.md` unchanged until `--yes`.
- `progress start-task` does not pass a new since, so the time stays.
- A task that says `(after: PR 87)` or `after PR 87 merges` stays held until the host says PR 87 is merged, and the walk ending says `waits for PR 87 to merge`.

## Choice words
- question: Do this step
  - `yes`: do the write, push, open, or merge just shown
  - `stop`: do not do it
  - `release-claim`: clear this branch's In progress: claim, then commit and push claims.md after yes
- question: Whose branch
  - `switch`: build on the other person's branch, in other-owner mode
  - `own`: this branch is ours
- question: Pull request description
  - `edit-description`: change the other owner's pull request description, only because this run asked
called_by: Called by the user.
runs by itself: Opens `/crav1-build-tasks`, `/crav1-verify-build-against-spec`, `/crav1-finalize-commit`, `/crav1-open-pr`, and `/crav1-merge-pr` by file and follows them. It does not start those slash commands. In other-owner mode it does not open the pull-request or merge skills.
you run next: /crav1-build-walk; /crav1-verify-build-against-spec
first: `/crav1-build-walk @docs/specs/<slug>/`
walkthrough: from-build-walk.md
